text: hey everybody any attempt to discover any  single biblical concept of marriage or of
masculinity or of Christianity or of anything  like that is absolutely inevitably a process
of negotiation with the text where certain  texts and certain readings of those texts
are centered and other texts are marginalized  or ignored or reinterpreted in service of those
texts that are centered and there are a couple  reasons for this one is that the Bible has no   single unified consistent perspective on any  of these ideologies that are at all relevant
to today and another is just the inevitability  of having to negotiate with text interpretation
is not a process of discovery it's a process  of creation where we bring interpretive lenses
to the text to engage in that negotiation  and if you're not careful you're primarily
going to be centering your own needs and  exigencies and circumstances and so when
we try to create some biblical concept of  marriage or of Christianity or of masculinity
in that negotiation the biblical text does not  take priority it is primarily the authorization
it is our proof text the priority is pretty much  always going to be how useful or meaningful that
reading is going to be to our structuring of power  and values in the service of our identity politics
